causes.text: On 30 July 2024, Pfizer's chief U.S. commercial officer announced that the company had significantly strengthened its contracting position with retail pharmacies for its respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine, Abrysvo, beginning in August. This move signalled an aggressive effort to challenge GlaxoSmithKline's dominance in RSV shots through new pharmacy contracts and improved retail shelf space.

source_info.title: RSV vaccine makers vying for market share in second year of shots

effects.text: On 31 July 2024, GSK cut its forecast for 2024 vaccine sales after quarterly revenue from its shingles vaccine Shingrix and RSV vaccine Arexvy missed expectations. The announcement unnerved investors and GSK's shares fell about 2.2% during the session, making it the biggest drag on London's FTSE 100 index.

source_info.title: GSK shares fall after sales of top two vaccines disappoint

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Pfizer's announcement of strengthened pharmacy contracts created an expectation that the company would quickly gain RSV vaccine shelf space. Investors interpreted this competitive escalation as a direct threat to GSK's hard-won market share in the U.S. pharmacies where Arexvy had dominated.

The prospect of pharmacies shifting to Pfizer's Abrysvo led analysts to warn that GSK's RSV sales momentum could stall. As news of the competitor's contracting gains circulated, sentiment toward GSK weakened and expectations for its 2024 vaccine revenue deteriorated.

When GSK reported disappointing sales the next day and cut its 2024 outlook, the heightened competitive anxiety translated into a sharp share-price decline. GSK's stock fell roughly 2.2%, reflecting investors' immediate reaction to both Pfizer's aggressive positioning and the weaker-than-expected sales figures.

rationale: Pfizer's strengthened pharmacy contracting positioned it to take away market share from GSK's Arexvy. Investors anticipated that GSK would lose pricing power and shelf presence, so when GSK confirmed softer vaccine sales and trimmed its forecast, the prior competitive warning amplified the sell-off.
counterfactual_analysis: Had Pfizer not announced more aggressive contracts, GSK's disappointing sales might have been perceived as an isolated issue rather than evidence of eroding market share. Without the competitive threat, the share price drop could have been more muted.

adversarial_confounders.text: Around the same time, Moderna's mResvia RSV vaccine gained U.S. approval and began shipping to retailers.
adversarial_confounders.impact: The entry of a third player could have contributed to investors reassessing RSV market dynamics and pressured GSK's valuation.

details.commentary: Pfizer's stronger pharmacy contracting for Abrysvo increased the bargaining power of large U.S. retailers over rival RSV suppliers. As shelf space and recommendation slots shifted toward Pfizer, GSK's vaccines faced tougher channel competition, putting pressure on its growth expectations.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Channel contracting and payer coverage
details.commentary: In the U.S. vaccine market, payer coverage and pharmacy contracts are crucial economic levers that determine how quickly new shots are adopted. Against that backdrop, Pfizer's contracting gains heightened concerns that GSK's RSV and shingles sales could undershoot prior hopes, contributing to the forecast cut and share price decline.
